chunks.text: Welcome to your agent teamwork upgrade! No artificial intelligence doctorate required. Imagine a tiny support team: one person keeps the goal straight, another investigates, another builds, and another reviews. We will give Copilot similarly clear jobs, rather than asking a crowd of helpers to change everything at once.

We will give Copilot similarly clear jobs, rather than asking a crowd of helpers to change everything at once.

chunks.text: Our practice app is an issue triage board with fictional support tickets. It is deliberately small. We will add priority, search, a summary, and an evidence export. The interesting part is how we direct the work, protect shared files, and check that the final result actually works.

chunks.text: This is a visual lesson with an artificial intelligence generated voice, not a recording of live product clicks. Pause whenever you want to try an example. The live workshop still lasts three hours: one hour of presentation and demonstrations, followed by two hours of hands-on labs.

chunks.text: Here is the whole workshop in three pieces. A custom agent is a reusable job description. A skill is a reusable recipe with supporting files. Your prompt is today's task: what to change, what to leave alone, and how to prove success. Different jobs need different tools, not bigger promises.

chunks.text: You will learn to give a helper a small, complete assignment. It needs the goal, the relevant context, the files it may edit, and the result to return. That result should contain evidence and unresolved questions. A confident sentence saying finished is not the same as a verified change.

chunks.text: You will also learn why two chats can collide in one repository. Separate conversations do not guarantee separate files. chunks.text: Lab one creates useful instructions, an agent, and a skill. Lab two delegates research and implements priority. Lab three coordinates search and summary without overlapping writers. Lab four reviews and exports evidence. Each lab has prompts, checkpoints, hints, and separate instructor answers, so you can recover without guessing.

chunks.text: A model proposes the next useful action. The harness is the control room around it: it supplies context, tools, permissions, and execution. A tool is an action such as reading a file or running a test. Changing the model does not automatically change the harness or its configuration format.

chunks.text: A custom agent is a definition of a specialist. A subagent is a helper doing delegated work in a separate context. You can select a specialist yourself, or a main agent can call it for a side task. Built-in helpers can be subagents too; you do not need a new profile for every task.

chunks.text: Context means the notes available to the helper. A session is an ongoing unit of work with its conversation and workspace. Two notebooks can sit on the same desk. Likewise, two separate contexts can still edit the same checkout. Keep the job definition, the delegated call, and the actual workspace separate in your thinking.

chunks.text: Here is our first collision. Two helpers have separate conversations, but both reach for the same file. One edit can overwrite the other. Subagents do not automatically get independent worktrees. A separate chat is useful for focus, but it is not evidence of filesystem isolation.

chunks.text: Three protections answer three different questions. A worktree separates working copies. Tool permissions control actions that need approval. A sandbox can restrict access to files, networks, or credentials. None is a substitute for the others. A worktree is another workbench, not a locked room around your computer.

chunks.text: Collisions are not limited to source code. Helpers in one checkout share its branch and Git index. Servers can fight over a port, and tests can overwrite a report directory. Before parallel writing, identify all the writable surfaces. If the boundaries are unclear, serialize the writes.
